_meta: iter 79: curated complexity-claim drills for Smell-test mode. Each entry pairs a lesson with its actual time complexity + a plausible-but-wrong distractor. The session randomly shows actual OR distractor as the 'claim'; user picks correct/wrong + sees the actual either way. Trains the interview reflex 'does the stated complexity match the code?' — graded heavily but never trained in isolation.

two-sum.note: Single pass with a hash map; complement check is O(1) amortized.

valid-palindrome.note: Two pointers walk the string once; alphanumeric filter is per-char O(1).

p-bfs.note: Each node enqueued once, processed once.

binary-search.note: Each iteration halves the search space.

p-3sum.note: Sort is O(n log n); the outer loop × inner two-pointer pass is O(n²).

p-merge-intervals.note: Sort dominates; the merge pass after sorting is O(n).

p-min-window.note: Each character entered and exited the window at most once; amortized linear.

valid-parentheses.note: Single pass over the string with O(1) stack push/pop per char.

p-contains-dup.note: Hash-set seen-check is O(1) amortized; single linear pass.

p-anagrams.note: Sort each of n words of length k as the hash key; map ops are O(1) amortized.
